lydia (People Ops): quick Q from an IC: they want to do an in-plan Roth conversion of some pre-tax 401(k) money. can someone outline vendor steps, tax withholding, payroll codes, and any impact on match/vesting? tagging @noah and @sam :wave:
noah (Benefits): short: in-plan Roth conversion is a taxable event (you convert pre-tax to Roth in the plan). taxes owed on converted amount in the year of conversion. vendor (AcmeRetire) supports in-plan conversions but requires a conversion request form.
sam (Payroll): operationally: payroll doesn't withhold tax automatically for a conversion unless employee requests withholding and vendor provides withholding instructions. usually it's reported as a taxable distribution/conversion on year-end forms. timing matters for year-of-income recognition.
noah (Benefits): details to flag:
- Conversion amount becomes taxable income (subject to federal/state income tax and applicable employee payroll taxes).
- It's not a distribution to the individual (stays in plan), so 10% early distribution penalty shouldn't apply as long as it's an in-plan conversion (but confirm with vendor).
- Employer match: converting pre-tax balance doesn't change employer matching policy. match is based on contributions, not conversions.
- Vesting: conversions operate on vested balance. you can only convert vested portion per plan rules.
raj: does AcmeRetire allow voluntary withholding from pay to cover the tax bill?
noah (Benefits): AcmeRetire can either: apply withholding at conversion if participant elects (some vendors allow mandatory withholding for distributions, conversions may be handled differently), or the participant can choose to adjust W-4 withholdings or make estimated tax payments. We usually recommend consulting a tax advisor.
sam (Payroll): Ops checklist for employee and payroll:
1) Employee completes AcmeRetire "In-Plan Roth Conversion" request via portal: https://portal.acmeretire.example (choose conversion amount).
2) AcmeRetire sends confirmation with transaction ID and indicates whether they will withhold taxes and what code to use. employee should save that email.
3) If vendor withholds, employee forwards vendor confirmation to payroll@redwood.example with subject: "AcmeRetire conversion - [Name] - [ID]" before payroll cutoff. payroll will apply vendor-provided withholding code if applicable.
4) If vendor does NOT withhold, employee can: (a) increase W-4 withholding, (b) make estimated tax payments, or (c) request voluntary supplemental withholding via payroll with code `ACME_OTH_TAX`—but payroll can only act on a vendor instruction or employee W-4 change.
5) Payroll coding: vendor conversion typically uses `ACME_401K_CONV` (taxable amount) and `ACME_401K_WHT` if withholding requested. include Acme transaction ID in ticket.
noah (Benefits): Extra notes:
- Conversion recognized in the calendar year the vendor posts the transaction; year-end reporting will reflect it on the 1099-R box as a taxable conversion (vendor does most reporting).
- If employee is concerned about the tax hit, consider partial conversions over multiple years to spread tax liabilities.
- Outstanding loans: conversions don't repay loans; check vendor rules if you have an outstanding loan because it can affect available vested balance.
raj: what about Roth 401k catch-up / after-tax contributions interplay?
noah (Benefits): Roth catch-up contributions are separate. In-plan conversions apply to pre-tax or after-tax amounts per plan rules. If you have after-tax non-Roth money, Acme may allow conversion of that to Roth in-plan (check portal).
